# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 47 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_047_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 4 — Spiritual Warfare and the Devil's Fear of the Righteous

**47:1** "I asked him again about the commandments, whether the commandments given could also be kept by those who are in the world." He said: "They can be kept. For I have commanded and given them over to you who are of the world. But I say to you, if you keep them and do not add any evil desires to them, you will live. But if you add even a little of the desires of the world, you will not be able to keep these commandments."

**47:2** He said to me further: "I shall make known to you also the works of the devil's deeds, since he also has works that are evil. When the man who is righteous comes, the devil is afraid of him. But when the man who is double-minded and weak comes, the devil is not afraid of him, but immediately enters into him."

**47:3** "The man who is full of faith is valiant against the devil and is not afraid of him. For he has the Lord with him, and has the power of God. But the double-minded man is afraid of the devil and comes easily under his influence, for the devil enters into that man and does whatever he wills with him."

**47:4** "But the Lord is the Angel of Righteousness and he strengthens all believers in faith and in doing good. Trust him and you shall overcome the devil, for the devil has no power at all to do anything to you. Only believe in God and trust him. Therefore also the Lord will come and will drive out the devil from among you, and will remove his power from you."

**47:5** "But the devil has a place to live and dwell only among those who are double-minded — the waverers who are afraid of him and have abandoned their faith. So the devil turns back to them and enters them and does every evil work. For those who have faith in their hearts, the devil cannot withstand. Therefore the commandment has this power: that the one who believes in God and does good shall have great joy."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the spiritual warfare imagery and the double-mindedness theology of the Mandates.*
